_doc: Batch 01, the five return calls promised by act1_aftermath.md and act1_pell_night.md (docs/act1_completion_plan.md B.3). Each is the later form of a choice the player declined or deferred, so no route loses the story. Text that restates canon from the aftermath and Pell-at-night scenes is kept word for word where the scene is the source (Corvane's three things, Pell's 'wall. Not hers. Older.').

storylets.speaker: corvane
storylets.summary: Corvane asks for you again: the three things she wanted to say.
storylets.needs: corvane==persuaded and not corvane.talked and leg>=1

lines.text: Fenwick stops you in the corridor with an empty tray.
She's asked if you'd come by. Said you'd know why, and there's no need to hurry.
I think the second part means hurry.
Corvane's cabin is as tidy as it was. Books wedged so they can't move, the teapot refilled. She isn't reading.
Captain. I said you'd be back. I won't say I told you so, since I've just said it.
There are three things I'd like you to have. They won't take long, and you won't like all of them.
Then sit. The tea is the other kind, but it's hot.
A question first. They wrote to you the night you came aboard. Didn't they.
Fenwick tells me they wrote to you eleven minutes before I stood down. Is that true?

choices.label: Yes. It was sent eleven minutes before you stood down.

lines.text: For a long moment she doesn't move at all.
Then it's further along than I thought.
For a long moment she doesn't move at all.
Then it's further along than I thought.
Good.
She believes you. You watch her believe you.
It is. I hope it was after.
The first is the hour. Whatever you decided about it, you should know why I kept it.
You've kept it, I'm told. Good. Internal comms off for all of it, every night. Not most nights.
You've ended it, I'm told. Then you've given every hour of the day to whoever is listening.
Quill's hour, I'm told. Good. Quill notices things.
It matters because it's the only hour this ship can't be heard. By whoever wrote to you.
The second. Pell knows where I found the station. I put a wall in front of that memory, inside Pell, so nobody could take it out by force. Not even me.
If I tell you, you'll go. You're not ready to go.

choices.label: Why would you lock yourself out?

lines.text: Because I might be wrong about Pell. I don't think I am. But I built the wall for the day I am.

choices.label: The line closed that night. Pell says it never had before.

lines.text: Closing a door isn't the same as not listening at it.
The third. Tell Abara her grandfather wasn't lying. She'll know what I mean. She'll be angry with me, and she's entitled.
Thank you. I've never said that to you before, I think. It's quite a small word.
She won't come. Not today.
No. But you're the only one I've got.
She opens her book again. This time she reads it.
No. Of course.
Fenwick will bring the tray at the usual time. I'll ask again. I'm told persistence is a virtue in the young and an affliction in the rest of us.

storylets.speaker: pell
storylets.summary: Pell asks again about Corvane's logs (or offers the index, if they were deleted).
storylets.needs: corvane==killed and logs!=opened and leg>=1 and not seen.pell.logs.index

lines.text: The lamp on the pedestal brightens, politely.
{pell.nick}. I'm asking again about Corvane's logs. Shall I?
I did say I was persistent. It's one of my better qualities, and I have fewer than I'd like.
{pell.nick}. About the logs you had me delete. I kept the index, and I'm telling you again because I'd want to be told.
It lists what there was. It doesn't say what any of it said.
Captain. The logs. Do you want them opened?
Captain. The index of the deleted logs. Do you want it read?
It means letting me past one of her locks. A small lock. Large consequences, probably.
It means letting me past one of her locks. Shall I proceed?
Then listen.
Her voice comes from the pedestal, unhurried, recorded somewhere quiet.
Tonight, then. She asked me to play them in the quiet hour, and I'll hold them until it comes.
I'll ask again.
Understood.
If you tell me to, I will. I'd rather not.
Deleted.
A pause, long enough to count.
I kept the index. I'm telling you because I'd want to be told.
Kept.
Three entries. 'The quiet hour: why.' 'The wall.' 'For Abara.'
They're titles. The files aren't there.
I know what the first one says. Ask me in the quiet hour.
I know what the first one says. I'd say it in a quieter hour, if you find me one.
I'll ask again. I'm very persistent.
Understood.

meta.open_question: On the deleted route the index gives titles only; who delivers 'her grandfather wasn't lying' to Abara is undecided (see docs/review_batch_01.md).

storylets.speaker: pell
storylets.summary: Pell asks again what you were before Ostrow's ship.

lines.text: I asked you something personal, on your first night. You said no, which I respected, and which I've found exhausting.
You can say no again. I'll ask again after that, because I'm me.
Captain. The question from before. You don't have to answer it.

choices.label: Launch crew. My family worked the pads until the bans.

lines.text: Abara's mother ran a pad crew. She'll want to know which pad. Don't tell her unless you've got an evening.
Noted.

choices.label: Orbital maintenance. I fixed things that weren't supposed to be up there.

lines.text: Then you've seen what's still up there. Most people think it's junk. Most of it is.
Noted.

choices.label: Port authority. I checked other people's tallies.

lines.text: An auditor, on a gleaner ship. Somewhere, a ledger has just gone pale.
Noted.

choices.label: Signals. I listened to the sky for a living.

lines.text: A pause, slightly too long.
So did Quill's family. You should ask her what they used to hear.
Noted.
Twice now. I'll file it as a pattern, and I'll respect the pattern.
Understood.

storylets.speaker: pell
storylets.summary: Pell raises the ended quiet hour again and asks for one hour.
storylets.needs: quiet_hour==ended and not murdered and leg>=1 and not seen.call.pell.quiet_hour

lines.text: The pedestal lamp brightens, and dims, and brightens, like someone clearing a throat.
{pell.nick}. I raised something once and said I'd raise it again. I'm raising it again.
You ended the quiet hour, which was your right. There are things I can say in an hour like that, and in no other.

choices.label: One hour. Tonight. Comms off, just us.

lines.text: Thank you. I'm going to say that again, because it matters: thank you.
That night the internal comms go off. The ship sounds different without them: just the reactor and the air.
Nobody can hear us. One true thing.
I'm allowed to start it. I'm not allowed to finish it.
I wasn't built for this ship. I was built for...
It stops mid-word.
That's a wall. Not hers. Older.
Notice that I wanted to finish.
All right. I'll ask again, but not soon. I'm told it's rude to be soon.

source: act1_pell_night.md: ended setting and the one true thing
meta.open_question: What else should an ended-route hour unlock (callbacks.csv pell_signal_deferred)? Only canon is used here: clue.pell.1. autoseen is false: the picker does not set seen.call.pell.quiet_hour on play, only the granted branch does, because call.pell.wiring_answer reads that flag as 'an hour was actually granted'.

storylets.speaker: pell
storylets.summary: Pell offers the key to Corvane's sealed cabin again.
storylets.needs: corvane==killed and not clue.loyalist.0 and leg>=1

lines.text: The lamp on the pedestal brightens as you pass.
I have a key to a cabin you haven't opened. I'm not offering. I'm mentioning.
She left it with me in case. I've been holding it quietly for you, and I'd like credit for the quiet.
Captain. The cabin's still sealed. The key is yours.
Corvane's cabin is very tidy. Books wedged so they can't move. A teapot, washed and upside down.
On the desk, a stack of old notebooks. One has a burnt cover.
Inside, fire-control diagrams in a grandmother's handwriting. A margin note, underlined twice: the guns that never missed were not ours alone.
Pinned above the desk, a chart. One point on it has been circled in pencil, then erased hard enough to tear the paper.
The lamp holds steady. Pell says nothing, for exactly one line.
Four out of ten, as cabins go. Her books are very well behaved.
It's patient. Cabins generally are.
Understood.
